::: {#rem-symmetry-breaking}

#### Random starting weights break the symmetry

Drawing the starting weights at random makes each [unit](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-unit) start as a different function,
so the [unit](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-unit)s receive different [gradients](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient) and can learn different [features](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/anatomy.html#def-feature)
[@goodfellow2016deep, section 8.4].
The biases can start at 0,
since the random weights already tell the [unit](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-unit)s apart.
@sol-init-scale and @sol-default-init then set the scale of the random weights.

:::
